title: Seven years, 29 moments
lede: From an AngelList posting to a shutdown notice. Filter by thread.

events.title: The idea surfaces
events.text: The Verge reports on a $99 hackable Android console designed by Yves Béhar, from a startup led by Julie Uhrman.

events.title: Kickstarter opens
events.text: The goal is $950,000. The campaign passes $1 million in about eight hours.

events.title: Kickstarter closes
events.text: $8,596,474 from 63,416 backers. Consoles are promised to backers by March 2013.

events.title: Developer consoles ship
events.text: The first units go to backers of the developer tiers.

events.title: Retailers and price named
events.text: Amazon, Best Buy, GameStop and Target will sell the console at $99.99 from June.

events.title: Backers’ consoles start shipping
events.text: The Kickstarter edition begins to go out.

events.title: Engadget: “a beta release”
events.text: The first major review says the backers’ machine is “simply not ready for retail.”

events.title: The Verge: 3.5 out of 10
events.text: Retail launch is then planned for June 4.

events.title: $15 million round
events.text: Kleiner Perkins leads; Mayfield, Nvidia, Shasta and Occam join. The retail launch moves three weeks to June 25.

events.title: Retail launch
events.text: On sale in the U.S., Canada and the U.K. Amazon sells out the same day.

events.title: Reviews average 62
events.text: A roundup of 12 critic and 9 user scores for the retail unit.

events.title: NPD: “relatively light”
events.text: The retail tracker’s assessment of the first month in U.S. stores, excluding ouya.tv sales.

events.title: Developers publish sales
events.text: TowerFall: about 2,000 copies. NimbleBit: 122 purchases from 6,508 downloads.

events.title: “Better than we expected”
events.text: Uhrman says 27% of owners have paid for a game and describes the $1 million Free the Games Fund.

events.title: Gridiron Thunder funded
events.text: The football game closes at $171,009 from 183 backers, and questions follow.

events.title: Developers pull games
events.text: Uhrman’s response to the fund controversy is badly received. Sophie Houlden removes Rose and Time.

events.title: Fund rules rewritten
events.text: Minimum cut from $50,000 to $10,000; PC release allowed; $100,000 bonus scrapped.

events.title: PlayStation 4 launches
events.text: Sony reports 1 million sold in North America in the first 24 hours.

events.title: Ouya Everywhere
events.text: The store will run on other companies’ hardware. Mad Catz’s M.O.J.O. is the first partner.

events.title: Amazon Fire TV
events.text: Amazon launches a $99 television box with a $39.99 game controller.

events.title: 7,000 copies
events.text: TowerFall’s creator says that is about what the best-selling Ouya game sold on Ouya.

events.title: Live on M.O.J.O.
events.text: The Ouya storefront arrives on Mad Catz’s $199 micro-console.

events.title: Alibaba invests $10 million
events.text: The aim is to bring Ouya’s library to Alibaba’s set-top box in China.

events.title: For sale
events.text: Fortune reports that Ouya tripped a covenant on TriplePoint debt and has hired Mesa Global to find a buyer.

events.title: Razer deal closes
events.text: Razer acquires the catalogue, the store and the team, not the hardware. Terms undisclosed.

events.title: Deal confirmed, Uhrman leaves
events.text: Razer announces the acquisition. The founder says goodbye on Twitter.

events.title: Razer picks up the fund
events.text: Razer says it will honour the $620,000 still unpaid from the Free the Games Fund, on modified terms.

events.title: Shutdown notice
events.text: Razer says the Ouya, Forge TV and M.O.J.O. stores will close in five weeks.

events.title: Switched off
events.text: Accounts are deactivated and the store and website go dark.
